summary:
Kırklareli Province has no province-specific statute, ordinance, enforcement pattern or incident series in the record. The position of a trans visitor in Kırklareli is set entirely by Turkey's national framework, and no Kırklareli-specific deviation from that framework is documented.

Homosexuality has not been a criminal offence in Turkey since the Ottoman Empire adopted a new penal code in 1858, and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender, after surgery, since 1988.

Turkey has no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity. LGBTQ people are barred from serving openly in the military, and same-sex relationships receive no legal recognition, including marriage, civil union and adoption.

Authorities have banned Pride events in Istanbul and other cities in most years since 2015, using tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions against participants.

In ILGA-Europe's 2026 Rainbow Europe ranking Turkey placed 47th out of 49 assessed countries.
